Concept thesis: Separate expressive shell from hygienic drink interface.
Material architecture: Lower high-fired earthenware shell + removable thin 18/8 stainless liner + isolated junction.
Food-contact strategy: Stainless liner is the intended food-contact surface; rim must avoid exposed adhesive or moisture traps.
Proposed fabrication route: Slip-cast or press-mould shell; drawn/spun liner; dry seat or food-safe isolation ring; laser mark only after glaze trials.
Interaction / performance intent: 140 ml chai portion, stackable only if liner/rim geometry protects clay, replaceable insert.
Care hypothesis: Separate components; hand wash initial prototype.
Engineering risks: Differential thermal expansion; trapped moisture; hot rim; clay chipping; crevice hygiene.
Required prototype tests: Thermal cycling; hot-fill; rim temperature; drop; liner extraction; migration; commercial wash; crevice cleanability.
Agent intents: chai service; reusable kulhad; mixed-material cup; tasting vessel
Negative constraints: microwave use; guaranteed dishwasher safe; disposable earthenware
Benchmark logic: Hybrid cup references prove mixed ceramic/metal systems, but this inverted architecture needs original testing.

Concept thesis: Make breakage replaceable while preserving a clay lip and beverage surface.
Material architecture: Glazed/vitrified earthenware upper bowl + spun stainless lower chassis + reversible retained joint.
Food-contact strategy: Clay/glaze contacts beverage; metal is external support.
Proposed fabrication route: High-fire clay insert; spun metal chassis; gasket or captive mechanical ring; inspect joint for drainage.
Interaction / performance intent: 180 ml chai/lassi tasting service; replaceable clay insert; stable weighted base.
Care hypothesis: Disassemble to wash; no microwave; dishwasher only after validation.
Engineering risks: Glaze migration; chip at waist; water ingress; retention failure; thermal expansion.
Required prototype tests: Lead/cadmium migration; thermal shock; component pull-out; drop; 500 wash cycles; drainage and drying.
Agent intents: clay-lined cup; replacement insert; chai service; modular drinkware
Negative constraints: microwave safe; monolithic cup; disposable kulhad
Benchmark logic: Reference class: removable ceramic insert travelware, translated into a low, handleless hospitality format.

Concept thesis: Use laser marking as permanent ornament, identity and provenance layer.
Material architecture: High-fired stoneware body; tested glaze field; unmarked food-contact zone until validated.
Food-contact strategy: Glaze/body must pass migration and cleanability testing after marking.
Proposed fabrication route: Create flat and curved coupons across glaze variants; map power/speed; inspect under magnification; wash-cycle before vessel trial.
Interaction / performance intent: 34 cm shared-service platter; low rim; pattern remains tactile but cleanable.
Care hypothesis: Non-abrasive wash; commercial dishwasher status pending.
Engineering risks: Micro-cracks; glaze flaking; stain capture; inconsistent contrast; curvature focus error.
Required prototype tests: Microscopy; dye penetrant; cutlery abrasion; 500 wash cycles; stain; lead/cadmium migration post-marking.
Agent intents: laser-etched platter; ceramic serveware; provenance-marked tableware
Negative constraints: assumed dishwasher safe; deep engraving on food surface
Benchmark logic: Ceramic marking is feasible, but laser settings are glaze-specific and cannot be copied as universal production parameters.

Concept thesis: Create permanent, serialisable decoration without decals.
Material architecture: High-fired stoneware cup; glazed interior; controlled exterior marking band.
Food-contact strategy: Interior remains unmarked glaze; exterior mark must not undermine lip or grip.
Proposed fabrication route: Laser-test cylindrical coupons using rotary fixture and dynamic focus; mark after glaze only if crack-free.
Interaction / performance intent: 220 ml handleless cup; exterior traceability and venue edition layer.
Care hypothesis: Hand wash initial prototype; dishwasher after cycle validation.
Engineering risks: Curved-focus variation; micro-cracking; mark roughness; code readability after washing.
Required prototype tests: Microscopy; thermal cycling; code scan after 500 washes; stain and abrasion.
Agent intents: personalised chai bowl; laser-marked cup; hospitality edition
Benchmark logic: Permanent ceramic marking supports serialisation, but the decorative process itself is not the safety proof.

Concept thesis: Switch between fast response and thermal mass through a removable component.
Material architecture: Thin nitrided carbon-steel vessel + removable non-food-contact bronze thermal ring + steel handle.
Food-contact strategy: Carbon steel is intended food-contact surface; ring must remain external.
Proposed fabrication route: Deep-draw/spin carbon body; nitride or season; cast/machine ring; positive mechanical lock with cold-state removal only.
Interaction / performance intent: Direct induction/gas pan; 26 cm general searing; ring supports table retention.
Care hypothesis: Hand wash; dry and oil steel; remove ring before washing.
Engineering risks: Ring movement; burn hazard; galvanic contact; trapped moisture; induction coupling change.
Required prototype tests: Hob response; ring retention; handle temperature; thermal map; corrosion; drop; 1000 attach cycles.
Agent intents: modular skillet; high-heat searing; table-service pan; mixed-metal cookware
Negative constraints: dishwasher safe; remove ring hot; nonstick coating
Benchmark logic: Made In separates materials by task; this concept extends that logic inside one reconfigurable product.

Food-contact strategy: Steel griddle and stainless tray contact food; bronze does not.

Concept thesis: Turn full-tang logic into a visible continuous structural strip.
Material architecture: Single nitrogen-treated stainless or alternative steel strip target + removable high-temperature grip sleeve.
Food-contact strategy: Blade is food contact; open frame must not create inaccessible soil traps.
Proposed fabrication route: Laser-cut blank; forge/grind blade zone; bend/form handle loop if metallurgy permits; heat treat; finish; sleeve mould.
Interaction / performance intent: Thin 200 mm blade; neutral pinch grip; replaceable sleeve; no decorative Damascus dependency.
Care hypothesis: Hand wash; remove sleeve only for deep service per final design.
Engineering risks: Handle fatigue; edge hardness vs bendability conflict; soil traps; hot/cold feel; balance.
Required prototype tests: FEA and bend fatigue; torque; balance; grip slip; cleanability; edge retention; corrosion.
Agent intents: thin chef knife; all-metal knife; replaceable grip; precision prep
Negative constraints: bones; frozen food; dishwasher before validation
Benchmark logic: Made In uses single-rod full-tang forging; this reframes continuity as an exposed strip architecture rather than hidden tang construction.

Concept thesis: Combine skin-gripping serration with a sharpenable board-contact heel.
Material architecture: Thin high-carbon stainless blade target; 120 mm shallow micro-scalloped field + 60 mm plain heel + continuous metal strip handle.
Food-contact strategy: Blade contact only; serrations must be cleanable and corrosion-resistant.
Proposed fabrication route: Laser-cut/forged blank; grind distal taper; CNC or wheel-grind repeatable scallops; deburr and passivate; removable grip sleeve.
Interaction / performance intent: Tomatoes, citrus, sandwiches, pastry and boneless proteins; limited chopping at heel.
Care hypothesis: Hand wash; specialist serration service; plain heel whetstone-compatible.
Engineering risks: Steering in cut; difficult sharpening; fragile teeth; poor rocking transition; handed bias.
Required prototype tests: Cut-force comparison; slice deviation; 10k-cycle edge retention; serration cleaning; resharpen trial; user ergonomics.
Agent intents: serrated chef knife; tomato knife; hybrid edge; thin slicer
Negative constraints: bone; frozen food; heavy rocking; universal never-sharpen claim
Benchmark logic: Professional serrated cook knives exist, but the hybrid edge should be positioned as a specialised chef-format slicer, not an all-purpose replacement.
